Title: [General Specification Policy] Approved Versions of the FHIR Standard
Requirement:
FHIR Specifications and FHIR Solutions SHALL be based on the following versions of the HL7 FHIR standard: 
  • 4.0.1 — HL7 Fast Healthcare Interoperability Resources, Release 4 (R4)
Rationale:
HL7 FHIR R4 (4.0.1) — an HL7 International Mixed Normative and Standard for Trial Use (STU) — is the most widely adopted version of FHIR globally and in Australia.  

Further, the NCTS is based on FHIR R4 and the HL7 Australia AU Base FHIR IG as well as all the FHIR IGs developed under the Sparked program are based on FHIR R4. Informative notes

HL7 FHIR R5 (5.0.0) — an HL7 International Standard for Trial Use (STU) — is currently the official version of FHIR. 

HL7 FHIR R6 is currently under development and may be released in 2026.

Title: [General Specification Policy] FHIR Specifications
Requirement: FHIR Specifications SHALL be developed and published as FHIR Implementation Guides.
Rationale: FHIR implementation guides are the standard mechanism for documenting FHIR Solutions – including their supported resource profiles, interactions, capabilities, and system behaviour.
Informative Note: A FHIR implementation guide (IG) is a set of rules concerning how the FHIR standard (including FHIR resource types and the RESTful API) are used to provide a solution for a particular problem including associated documentation to support and clarify the usage.

Title: [General Specification Policy] Development and publication of FHIR Specifications as FHIR IG
Requirement: FHIR Specifications SHALL be developed and published as a FHIR Implementation Guide (FHIR IG) using the HL7 International FHIR IG Publisher.
Rationale: The HL7 International FHIR Implementation Guide Publisher (IG Publisher) is a widely used and trusted tool for developing and publishing FHIR Implementation Guides. Additionally, it performs complex validation of content in specifications leading to better quality and fewer technical errors in publication. Finally, given the broad adoption of IG Publisher-developed FHIR IGs in Australia and globally, FHIR implementers have become very adept at reading FHIR IGs produced using the IG Publisher.
Informative Note: The HL7 International Implementation Guide Publisher is an open-source Java application that processes the source code for a FHIR Implementation Guide and processes it to produce a published FHIR IG. The IG Publisher’s source code is available from GitHub in the HL7/fhir-ig-publisher repository.

Title: [General Specification Policy] Approved dependencies
Requirement: FHIR Specifications SHALL only reference approved dependencies from the Agency FHIR Registry (AFR).
Rationale: Dependencies (including terminology artefacts, FHIR artefacts or base standards) should only be used if they have been assessed as suitable for use in Agency specifications.
Informative Note: The Agency FHIR Registry (AFR) is a published list of approved FHIR specifications and artefacts (both internally and externally developed) for use by the Agency. The AFR is maintained by the FHIR Framework Group (FFG).  For more details, see FHIR Registry.

Title: [General Specification Policy] Experimental dependencies
Requirement: If FHIR specifications has any dependency on experimental artefact, then the specification SHALL explicitly provide narrative explaining the experimental artefact.
Rationale: Experimental dependencies (including terminology artefacts, FHIR extensions) should only be used if they have been assessed as suitable for use in Agency specifications and the implementers must be made aware of this.

Title: [General Specification Policy] Inclusion in FHIR Package Registry
Requirement: FHIR Implementation Guides (FHIR IGs) SHALL be packaged as FHIR NPM Packages and SHALL be published to the HL7 International FHIR Package Registry.
Rationale: It is standard practice for publicly accessible FHIR Implementation Guides to be packaged as a FHIR NPM Package and uploaded to the FHIR Package Registry.
Informative Note:
A FHIR Package is a collection of FHIR Resources (like a directory with a JSON file-per-resource). FHIR package management is based on the Node Package Manager (NPM) standard. The FHIR Package standard is currently a subset of the NPM standard. 
The FHIR Package Registry allows implementers to search through the thousands of resources created by the community and provides quick access to reference, download, and install.
Compliance Note: Whilst this requirement cannot be undertaken on assessment of the FHIR Specification itself (because it needs to pass assessment before it can be published), it is expected to be a follow-on action from a successful assessment of a submitted FHIR Specification, where the submitting team notify the FFG when the corresponding FHIR NPM Package has been added to the registry which the FFG can confirm.

Title: [General Specification Policy] Inclusion in FHIR Implementation Guide Registry
Requirement: FHIR Implementation Guides (FHIR IGs) SHALL be published to the HL7 International FHIR Implementation Guide Registry.
Rationale: It is standard practice for publicly accessible FHIR Implementation Guides to be added to the Framework's Implementation Guide Registry.
Informative Note: The FHIR Implementation Guide Registry provides a consolidated list of implementation guides defined by the FHIR community.
Compliance Note: Whilst this requirement cannot be undertaken on assessment of the FHIR Specification itself (because it needs to pass assessment before it can be published), it is expected to be a follow-on action from a successful assessment of a submitted FHIR Specification, where the submitting team notify the FFG when the corresponding FHIR IG has been added to the Implementation Guide Registry which the FFG can confirm.

Title: [General Specification Policy] Publication of terminology artefacts in the National Clinical Terminology Service
Requirement: Terminology artefacts (including CodeSystem, ValueSet, and ConceptMap FHIR resource instances) SHALL be published through the National Clinical Terminology Service (NCTS) and made discoverable through the HL7 International Terminology Ecosystem.
Rationale: Publication in the NCTS allows these resources to be easily discovered (via the NCTS Website), distributed (via the NCTS National Syndication Service) and made available through the HL7 International Terminology Ecosystem.
Informative Note: The NCTS is a national digital health service provided by the Australian Digital Health Agency to facilitate the effective use adoption of clinical terminology content products like SNOMED CT-AU.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Canonical Base
Requirement:
FHIR conformance resources defined in a FHIR Specification SHALL use a canonical base URI structured in the following format: 

http://digitalhealth.gov.au/fhir/[ig-acronym]/ 

Where: 
  • [ig-acronym] is the acronym of the specific Implementation Guide.
Rationale: The canonical base is used when populating the url value of resources as per resource-specific policy requirements.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Name
Requirement:
The name data element of the resource SHALL have a short and descriptive value and only be composed of a combination of: 
  • upper and lower-case alphabetic characters; and 
  • numeric characters; and 
  • underscore (‘_’) to separate words
Rationale: The use of underscores (‘_’) in the ‘name’ element enables efficient computer processing during IG generation and provides better readability.
Informative Note: The FHIR standard allows this value to have a maximum of 254 characters.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource File Name
Requirement:
The convention for name of FHIR resource file SHOULD follow the format: [resource-type]-[name]-[version].[file-extension].  
Where: 
  • [resource-type] is the FHIR resource type; and 
  • [name] is the value of the resource’s name element; and  
  • [version] is the artefact version 
  • [file-extension] is either 
    • xml for XML formatted files; or 
    • json for JSON formatted files.
Rationale: This helps maintain consistency while exporting FHIR resources as files and aligns with organisational standards to maintain consistency across teams.
Informative Note: The file naming conventions may change based on the tool used to author the content and configuration settings within the IG publisher.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Title
Requirement:
The title element of the resource SHALL be a completely human readable description in title case, that is grammatically correct, preferably with full expansion of any abbreviations included in the name unless those expansions are foreign to readers. It may include a suffix in brackets for the variant. 
 
The resource’s title value SHALL follow the followings: 
  • be a completely human readable description in title case, that is grammatically correct. 
  • preferably with full expansion of any abbreviations included in the name unless those expansions are foreign to readers.
  • It may include a suffix in brackets for the variant.
Rationale: Serves as the human readable headline in generated docs, ensuring that the title is descriptive of what the resource is to aid in understanding and discovery
Informative Note:
For more information on ‘title case’ refer to the link:  
Sentence case, title case and the titles of works | Style Manual

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Status
Requirement: The status element of the resource SHALL be set to ‘active’ for final publication.
Rationale: This field is used to track the life-cycle status of the resource.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Experimental Resources
Requirement: The experimental element of the resource SHALL be set to ‘false’ for specifications.
Rationale: This Boolean flag specifies whether the resource has been created solely for testing purposes, with no version of the resource intended for actual deployment or production use.
Informative Note: Specifications under development and not yet finalised may have the flag as ‘true’ for resources.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource date
Requirement: The date element of the resource SHALL include a value indicating when the resource was last changed using the format YYYY-DD-MM. The date SHALL be synced with the IG publication date.
Rationale: To ensure that implementers have clear visibility of the resource update date when the resource is accessed outside of the IG context.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Publisher
Requirement: The publisher element of the resource SHALL use “Australian Digital Health Agency".
Rationale: The publisher details help implementers assess the reliability of the information.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Contact
Requirement:
The contact element of the resource SHALL include the following contact details 
  • contact.name : Australian Digital Health Agency 
  • contact.telecom 
  • system : url 
  • value : https://www.digitalhealth.gov.au 
  • contact.telecom 
  • system : email 
  • value : help@digitalhealth.gov.au 
    mailto:help@digitalhealth.gov.au
Rationale: The contact information provides a direct and always reliable channels for readers, stakeholders, or users of the resource to reach out to the Agency with questions, feedback, or requests for clarification.
Informative Note: FHIR Specification authors may add additional content elements if required.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Description
Requirement: The description element of the resource SHALL include a value which provides a succinct and contextual human-readable description of the resource.
Rationale: The description of the resource gives readers a quick understanding of what the resource is, without needing to dig through technical details.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Jurisdiction
Requirement: Projects within the agency SHALL adopt UsageContext for IG publication. The value for the ‘jurisdiction’ SHALL be ‘urn:iso:std:iso:3166#AU "Australia"’
Rationale:
• Using UsageContext in the implementation Guide ensures the specification is future-proof. 
  • The jurisdiction details of a resource ensure the document aligns with relevant laws and regulations of the chosen jurisdiction, which may have unique requirements or policies.
Informative Note: The jurisdiction element has been deprecated in FHIR R5 in favour of using UsageContext.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Purpose
Requirement: The purpose element of the resource SHALL provide a value which summarises clear purpose, including a brief description of the business problem the resources aims to solve.
Rationale: This establishes the resource’s purpose and ensures appropriate expectations are set for its intended use.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Copyright
Requirement: The copyright element of the resource SHALL provide with the appropriate copyright statement as the value.
Rationale: This provides ownership clarity and relevant details around the public use and legal protection of the resource.
Informative Note: The copyright element has a datatype of Markdown and thus allows formatting of the copyright statement.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Version
Requirement:
The version element of the resource SHALL provide a value as per the defined versioning scheme in the specification. 
The version of the resources SHALL meet the following requirements: 
  • Terminology resource versions: The individual terminology artefacts (CodeSystem, ValueSet, ConceptMap) SHALL maintain their own version number which could be different than the IG version. 
  • Other resource version: The version of the IG SHALL be defaulted to all these non-terminology resources.
Rationale: Versioning enables a clear, auditable history of specification changes, ensuring that implementers know which version they are using and whether updates are available.
Informative Note: Use case specific resources always uses the IG version number.

Title: [FHIR Resource Conformance] Resource Change History
Requirement: Any changes to the IG artefacts SHALL be manually documented on a single page as a human readable change history within the Implementation Guide.
Rationale: The change history allows implementers to trace specific changes back to their implementation, which is crucial for auditing, compliance, and increases transparency.
Informative Note:
• The change log details provided in the IG are created following the minimal log pattern and styles used in AU Core and AU Base.   
  • Providing reference to any ticket number is optional. 
  • Where applicable, link to change history of the IG artefacts can be generated using the HL7 provided Implementation Guide tool

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Resource Id
Requirement:
The resource Id (logical identifier) of the Implementation Guide resource SHALL follow the format:  
au.gov.digitalhealth.fhir.[short-name] 
Where: 
[short-name] is the abbreviated name of the Implementation Guide.
Rationale: Consistent format of Resource Id makes the IG resource portable across environments (development, staging, production) provides a consistent way to form package-id for the implementation guide.
Informative Note:
• The resource id will be used as the package id of the IG and will be registered in the Agency FHIR package registry. 
  • The Resource id must be unique across implementation guides published by the Agency. 
  • Resource id doesn’t need to include the version of the FHIR used.

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/ImplementationGuide/[package-id] 
 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [package-id] is the id element of the ImplementationGuide resource.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the Implementation Guide ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the IG SHALL follow the format: [ig]_ImplementationGuide 
Where: 
  • [ig]: Represents short name specific to the FHIR Implementation Guide. Example: Use “PCA” as the prefix for Provider Connect Australia specific IG.
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern improves readability and interoperability.

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Resource Packaging
Requirement:
ImplementationGuides SHALL be packaged and published in the following ways: 
  • Use Case IG: All IG’s built based on any specific user case SHALL be packaged separately.  
  • Extension IG: All extensions used in various IGs SHALL be packaged and published as a dedicated extension IG pack. The extensions are referenced from various use case specific IGs. 
  • Terminology IG: The terminology artefacts which are not published as part of the Use Case specific IGs but deployed in NCTS server, SHALL be published within the Terminology IG.
Rationale: Establishing a clear and logical delineation of artefacts across respective IGs facilitates improved maintainability, streamlined packaging, and efficient publication.

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Resource Version
Requirement:
The version of the IG SHALL follow the following guidelines: 
  • Terminology IG: For terminology specific IG containing CodeSystem, ValueSet and ConceptMap SALL follow the HL7 THO approach in which a 3-part release version identifier, in the format of MAJOR.MINOR.BUILD is used.  
    • MAJOR: Major number indicates a new major release which may include breaking changes or substantial layout or formatting changes.   
    • MINOR: For all non-breaking changes which is a snapshot of the current build 
    • BUILD: Always fixed as ‘0’ (zero). 
  • Use Case IG:  All other conformant artefacts (e.g. ImplementationGuide, StructureDefinition, StructureMap etc) that are associated to the use case specific IG, SHALL follow the Semantic Versioning scheme where the standard MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (x.y.z) format is used for FHIR specification artifacts.  
    • MAJOR: This represents the year the artefact was released, in 'YY' format.   
    • MINOR: For all changes, both breaking and non-breaking changes. 
    • PATCH: Always fixed as ‘0’ (zero). . 
  • Version Change Rule: The following rules SHALL be followed for incrementing the version number for non-terminology resources.  
    • Non-substantive changes: Minor updates to metadata (like the author's name) don't require a version change.  
    • Strict changes: Any alteration to an artifact requires a version increment of the ‘y’ value in the ‘x.y.z’ scheme as mentioned above.
Rationale: IG versioning is critical for ensuring traceability, consistency, and control in the IG content, implementation, and relevant documentation management.

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Specification Extensibility
Requirement: Implementation Guides SHALL explicitly state whether they are an extensible (open) specification or not (closed).
Rationale: Without clarity on whether a specification is extensible, adopters of the specification may make an incorrect assumption leading to unpredictable and difficult to manage outcomes.
Informative Note:
The following points describe extensible and non-extensible specifications in this context:
  • Extensible or open specifications are those which allow adopters of the specification to extend the specifications beyond what is defined in the original specification and remaining conformant with the original specification. Examples include additional data elements in profiles, additional APIs operations (or operation parameters), and additional actor behaviours. 
  • Non-extensible or closed specifications are those which forbid adopters from extending the original specification and remaining conformant with the original specification.

Title: [FHIR ImplementationGuide] Extensible Specifications
Requirement: Extensible Implementation Guides SHALL explicitly state the rules and conditions for extensibility.
Rationale: Most open specifications will have limitations on the extent to which adopters can extend the specification. For example, the use of modifier FHIR extensions may be undesirable. It may also be desirable for FHIR extensions from trusted sources to be adopted.

Title: [FHIR StructureDefinition (Extension)] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/StructureDefinition/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the extension.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the agency defined extensions ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [FHIR StructureDefinition (Extension)] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the extension SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_[element-name(optional)]_[<use-case>] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: Represents short name specific to the FHIR Implementation Guide. Example: Use “MHR” as the prefix for all My Health Record specific extensions. 
  • [<element-name >]: name of the element in the FHIR resource. 
  • [<use case>]: describes the functional context of the extension. This could be individual words separated by ‘_‘ 
    • can be two or three and less than five words 
    • may contain common use abbreviations or acronyms
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined extensions promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [FHIR StructureDefinition (Profile)] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/StructureDefinition/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the extension.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the agency defined custom profiles ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [FHIR StructureDefinition (Profile)] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the profile SHALL follow the format: [ig]_[resource-type]_[use case (optional)]_[sub use case (optional)] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: Represents short name specific to the FHIR Implementation Guide. Example: Use “MHR” as the prefix for all My Health Record specific profiles. 
  • [<resource-type>]: This is the value in StructureDefinition.type, the FHIR resource type used in the profile. 
  • [<use case>]: While drafting any use-case specific profile, the use case can be included in the name. 
  • [<sub use case>]: Optionally, a sub use case name can be included if applicable.
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined custom FHIR profiles promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [FHIR CapabilityStatement] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/CapabilityStatement/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the capability statement.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the server’s capability statement ensures consistency and easy retrieval by the implementing software applications.

Title: [FHIR CapabilityStatement] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the capability statement SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_[<use case>(optional)]_CapabilityStatement 
Where: 
  • [ig]: represents specific IG. Example: Use “MOF” as the prefix for all My Health Record On FHIR specific profiles. 
  • [<use case>]: describes the functional context of the capability statement. 
  • Either the <ig> or the <user case> or both SHALL be present.
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for capability statement promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [FHIR SearchParameter] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/SearchParameter/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the search parameter.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the custom search parameter profiles ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [FHIR SearchParameter] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the capability statement SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_[<resource-type>]_[<use case>] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: represents specific IG. Example: Use “MOF” as the prefix for all My Health Record On FHIR specific profiles. 
  • <resource-type>: FHIR resource type. 
  • [<use case>]: describes the functional context of the search parameter
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined search parameters promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [FHIR OperationDefinition] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/OperationDefinition/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the operation.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the agency defined custom FHIR operations ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [FHIR OperationDefinition] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the capability statement SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_[<use case>] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: represents specific IG. Example: Use “MOF” as the prefix for all My Health Record On FHIR specific profiles. 
  • [<use case>]: describes the functional context of the operation
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined FHIR operations promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [CodeSystem] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/CodeSystem/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the CodeSystem. 
  • CodeSystem's identifier SHALL be aligned with the NCTS Complete Code System profile
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the CodeSystem resources ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [CodeSystem] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the CodeSystem SHALL follow the format: [<use-case>] 
Where: 
  • [<use case>]: describes the functional context of the code system
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined CodeSystem resources promotes improved readability and interoperability.
Informative Note: While the ValueSet name is typically suffixed from the IG name, the Code System name should remain more generic and does not require the IG in the name.

Title: [CodeSystem] NCTS Complete Code System Profile
Requirement: f the FHIR CodeSystem resource has a content element value of complete, it SHALL conform to the latest available version of the NCTS Complete Code System FHIR profile for FHIR R4.
Rationale: The NCTS Complete Code System FHIR profile ensures best practices are followed for CodeSystem resources that define complete code systems and better compatibility with the NCTS.
Informative Note: The url for the NCTS Complete Code System FHIR profile is https://healthterminologies.gov.au/fhir/StructureDefinition/complete-code-system-4

Title: [ValueSet] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/ValueSet/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the ValueSet.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the ValueSet resources ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [ValueSet] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the ValueSet SHALL follow the format: [ig]_[<use-case>] 
where 
  • [ig]: represents specific IG. Example: Use “MOF” as the prefix for all My Health Record On FHIR specific profiles. 
  • [<use case>]: describes the functional context of the value set
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined ValueSet resources promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [ValueSet] NCTS Composed Value Set profile
Requirement: If the FHIR ValueSet resource is a value set definition, it SHALL conform to version 4.1.0 of the NCTS Composed Value Set FHIR profile.
Rationale: The NCTS Composed Value Set FHIR profile ensures best practicses are followed for ValueSet definition resources and better compatibility with the NCTS.
Informative Note: The url for the NCTS Composed Value Set FHIR profile is https://healthterminologies.gov.au/fhir/StructureDefinition/composed-value-set-4

Title: [ConceptMap] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/ConceptMap/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the ConceptMap.
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the ConceptMap resources ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [ConceptMap] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the concept map SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_[<use-case>]_[<source concept standard>_To_<target concept standard>(optional)] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: Represents short name specific to the FHIR specification. Example: Use “MHR” as the prefix for all My Health Record specific ConceptMaps. 
  • [<use-case>]: describes the functional context of the ConceptMap.  
  • Optional Source and Target contexts: 
    • <source concept standard>: source concept systems name. e.g. HL7 v2 
    • <target concept standard>: target concept systems name. e.g. SNOMED-CT AU
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined ConceptMap resources promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [ConceptMap] Resource Example
Requirement:
The following additional policy requirements SHOULD be followed while providing ConceptMap specific examples: 
  • Provide example to demonstrate multiple sources and targets combination 
  • Provide example to demonstrate complex ConceptMap 
  • Provide separate examples to demonstrate the following relationship between source and target 
    • related-to 
    • equivalent  
    • source-is-narrower-than-target 
    • source-is-broader-than-target  
    • not-related-to
Rationale: Multiple examples of ConceptMap resources help implementers better understand how to use them.

Title: [ConceptMap] NCTS General Concept Map profile
Requirement: FHIR ConceptMap resources SHALL conform to version 4.0.0 of the NCTS General Concept Map FHIR profile.
Rationale: The NCTS General Concept Map FHIR profile ensures best practicses are followed for ConceptMap resources and better compatibility with the NCTS.
Informative Note: The url for the NCTS General Concept Map FHIR profile is https://healthterminologies.gov.au/fhir/StructureDefinition/general-concept-map-4

Title: [StructureMap] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/StructureMap/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the StructureMap
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the StructureMap resources ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [Structure Map] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the structure map SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_Transform_[<source structure>]_To_[<target structure>] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: Represents short name specific to the FHIR specification. Example: Use “MHR” as the prefix for all My Health Record specific StructureMaps. 
  • Source and Target structures: 
  • <source structure>: source StructureDefinition. e.g. ActivityDefinition 
  • <target structure >: target StructureDefinition. e.g. SupplyRequest
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined StructureMap resources promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [Structure Map] Resource Example
Requirement:
The following additional policy requirements SHOULD be followed while providing StructureMap specific examples: 
  • Provide example to demonstrate multiple sources and targets combinations 
  • Provide example to demonstrate complex StructureMap
Rationale: Multiple examples of StructureMap resources help implementers better understand how to use them.

Title: [Questionnaire] Resource Url
Requirement:
The url element SHALL be populated using a globally unique URI, structured in the following format: 
[base]/Questionnaire/[name] 
Where: 
  • [base] is the canonical base URI of the resource 
  • The [name] is the value of the name element of the Questionnaire
Rationale: A globally unique URI for the Questionnaire instances ensures consistency and alignment with the FHIR IG publication guidelines.

Title: [Questionnaire] Resource Name
Requirement:
The [name] of the Questionnaire SHALL follow the format: [ig (optional)]_[<use-case>] 
Where: 
  • [ig]: Represents short name specific to the FHIR specification. Example: Use “CHAP” as the prefix for all CHAP Questionnaire. 
  • [<use-case>]: describes the functional context of the Questionnaire.
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for agency defined Questionnaires promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [Questionnnaire] Limit Questionnaire Nesting Level
Requirement: Where possible, nested Questionnaire above 2 levels SHOULD be avoided.
Rationale:
Deep nesting can lead to: 
  • Increased complexity in rendering and user interface design. 
  • Difficulty in maintaining and validating the structure. 
  • Challenges in mapping responses to data models or clinical concepts and data extraction. 
  • Limiting levels helps optimise performance, especially in mobile or low-resource environments.
Informative Note: Where possible, apply SDC Questionnaire model.

Title: [Questionnaire] Support for Data Extraction
Requirement: The $extract operation and template extraction process SHOULD be leveraged to extract data where applicable.
Rationale:
Data extraction enables better use of the collected data and supports the followings: 
  • Clinical decision support  
  • Analytics  
  • Integration with EHRs or other systems
Informative Note:
• Minimising nesting in the Questionnaire resources in such a way so that specific answers can be extracted into other FHIR resources. 
  • Apply StructureMap based extraction where template extraction can’t be achieved.

Title: [Questionnaire] Multiple Language Support
Requirement: Where applicable, multi-language support for Questionnaire resources SHOULD be supported.
Rationale: Enabling multilingual support in Questionnaires enhances accessibility across diverse healthcare settings.
Informative Note:
• Leverage Resource.language and Human Language extension to support the language of the questionnaire content. 
  • Prefer using a ‘xml:lang’ attribute on a top-level ‘div’ within the Narrative section and display all the language so that language aware system can filter based on the logged in user’s language choice.

Title: [Questionanaire] Favour Simplicity
Requirement: Favour simplicity over complexity, where the same outcome can be achieved (e.g.: multiple enableWhen vs enableWhenExpression) and focus on the structure of Questionnaire than rendering.
Rationale: Simplicity is likely to be less compute intensive as well as being more readable to future authors.
Informative Note:
• In line with standard programming principles, variables must be declared before they are referenced.  
  • Where applicable, prefer using FHIRPath functions with the smallest footprint.

Title: [Questionnaire] Use of ValueSet
Requirement: ValueSet resources SHALL be used wherever lists of predefined Coding values are reused throughout a Questionnaire.
Rationale: Enhance re-usability, brevity and performance.
Informative Note: Using a ValueSet provides a reusable solution for populating dropdown lists with the same set of options across multiple questions.

Title: [Questionnaire] Choice Data Type Design
Requirement: ValueCoding resources SHALL be used for items of type Choice.
Rationale: Expressions using the answer can rely upon the code, and the display can be separated from the interactivity expressions. However, when using valueString, each of the dependant expressions need to also be updated when a small wording change is required by the business.
Informative Note: Using valueCoding can buffer against any possible wording changes to the possible answers.

Title: [Questionnaire] Use of Terminology Server
Requirement: Where possible, terminology resources used in the Questionnaire resources SHOULD be fetched from a terminology server than using it as contained resource.
Rationale: Decoupling the Questionnaire from the terminology resources offers greater flexibility and easier maintenance.
Informative Note: Prefer using valueCoding whiling designing items of type Choice.

Title: [Example] Must Include Example
Requirement: Each conformance resource in the specification SHALL include at least one example conformant to the specification in context.
Rationale: Inclusion of examples for each conformance resource in the specification ensures clarity in implementation.
Informative Note: Include Agency profile and specification conformant examples only. Avoid including examples for conformant resources that are derived from another implementation guide or specification.

Title: [Example] OperationDefintion Interaction Example
Requirement: Each OperationDefinition SHALL be accompanied by pairs of request and corresponding response examples which cover the distinct ways the operation can be invoked.
Rationale: OperationDefinition instances are not used to provide examples of custom operations or named queries; rather, they are included in the specification defined FHIR operations and named queries. Accordingly, conformant request and response examples better illustrate the correct implementation of the OperationDefinition.

Title: [Example] Example Coverage
Requirement: Examples provided in the specification SHOULD include coverage of real world usage scenarios, as applicable to the various profiles and extensions used in the specification.
Rationale: Providing consistent examples for all conformance resources in the specification offers clear implementation context.
Informative Note: An IG designed for multiple use cases should include examples that cover all relevant usage scenarios.

Title: [Example] Cover Must-Support Data Elements
Requirement: At least one example covering all mandatory and ‘Must-Support’ data elements SHALL be provided.
Rationale: Examples that include must-support enabled data elements serve to demonstrate compliance with the expected implementation obligations for the data elements in context.
Informative Note: Consider providing examples for ‘populate-if-known’ and ‘populate’ obligation tagged data elements.

Title: [Example] Cover Maximum Data Elements
Requirement: At least one example covering all mandatory, optional (as applicable) and extension data elements SHOULD be provided.
Rationale: A well-constructed, full-coverage example minimises the risk of implementation misinterpretation by showing how all elements interact in a real-world scenario.
Informative Note: When including optional data elements in the example, consider only those that are applicable to the profile in context. Do not include all optional elements defined in the International FHIR Specification.

Title: [Example] Meet Minimum Requirements
Requirement: At least one example covering only the mandatory elements SHALL be provided.
Rationale: Minimum requirements ensure that these examples are comprehensive enough to guide developers through common and edge-case scenarios.
Informative Note: Consider all elements and extensions having 1..* cardinalities in the specification.

Title: [Example] Provide Contextual Unambiguous Examples
Requirement: To reduce ambiguity and limit the number of examples included in the specification, more than one example for the same purpose and context SHOULD be avoided.
Rationale: Including too many examples may overwhelm implementers. A focused set of examples that highlight the key aspects of the implementation guide will offer sufficient context and clarity.
Informative Note: To ensure concise and focused documentation, avoid including multiple examples that illustrate the same data element.

Title: [Example] Provide Valid, Real-World Data
Requirement: The example provided in the specification SHALL include non-identifiable and non-production typical real-world data that reflects common clinically coherent, safe, and relevant scenarios.
Rationale: Including clinically safe and typical real-world examples in the specification enhances both the usability and trustworthiness of the standard in healthcare environments and helps implementers understand how to use FHIR resources without violating patient safety or privacy and avoid incorrect clinical interpretations.
Informative Note: Wherever appropriate, consider using publicly available test data sets while constructing examples.

Title: [Example] Provide Example Purpose
Requirement: The purpose of the example, along with detailing the use case context SHOULD be provided in the specification.
Rationale: The description and purpose of the example enhance clarity and relevance within in the specification and helps the reader understand why the example is being presented.
Informative Note: Use a short description outlining the use case context for each example included in the specification.

Title: [Example] Avoid Profile Assertion within Example
Requirement: Examples provided in the specification SHOULD NOT populate ‘meta.profile’ element.
Rationale: Examples play a key role in implementing the specification. Inclusion of ‘meta.profile’ may set an expectation that this tag must be populated in production instances, which is not recommended.
Informative Note: The IG development team are advised to Vvalidate the examples before including it in the specification using ‘compliesWithProfile’ extension.

Title: [Example] Example Validation
Requirement: Only the examples pre-validated using the HL7 FHIR validator SHALL be included in the specification.
Rationale: Inclusion of examples that are validated (e.g., required fields, valid values, expected behaviours) by the HL7 FHIR validator in the specification helps prevent incomplete or misleading implementations.
Informative Note: Use HL7 FHIR validation tool to validate the example.

Title: [Must Support & Obligation] Obligation & Must Support
Requirement: If the specification uses obligation, then the obligation SHALL be accompanied by an explicit must-support flag.
Rationale:
• Adding obligations to FHIR resources underpins conformance check and promotes semantic consistency. 
  • By enforcing consistent data structures and mandatory fields, obligations make it easier for systems to exchange and interpret data reliably enabling automated validation. 
  • Flagging an element with Must Support introduces conformance requirement for the use case in some meaningful way and clarifies how a system should produce or consume resources to support that element.
Informative Note:
• Obligation is fairly new concept in FHIR and being adopted Nationally and Internationally to as a better approach to specify conformance requirement for system behaviour. 
  • Use the obligation extension and use case aligned obligation code. 
  • Must Support along with related obligation provides clarify on the conformance requirements

Title: [Must Support & Obligation] Obligation Actor
Requirement:
• The specification SHALL define all the actors as applicable to the use case. 
  • The specification SHALL define obligations for all actors as applicable.
Rationale: Defining use case specific actors helps in clarify whether and how the obligation applies to the data sender, receiver, or both and reflects the real-world roles of these systems.
Informative Note: Actors related to obligation are specified using an ActorDefinition resource.

Title: [Missing Data & Suppressed Data] Support for Missing Data
Requirement: Support for missing data (i.e. where implementers are unable to provide a value for a mandatory or conditionally mandatory data element) SHALL be based solely on the corresponding business and information requirements which the specification is based upon.
Rationale: The Agency’s FHIR Specifications provide implementable technical specifications for well understood business and clinical use cases and their supporting technical documentation. These use cases are very likely to be sensitive to any missing data on the overall solution being supported. Accordingly, it is not up to teams responsible for developing the FHIR Specification to decide how and where missing data should be supported.
Informative Note: Teams responsible for developing FHIR Specifications are encouraged to ensure teams responsible for business and information requirements are aware of available approaches to supporting missing data in FHIR.

Title: [Missing Data & Suppressed Data] Missing Data Support in Dependencies
Requirement: Specifications which depend on other FHIR specifications (or Implementation Guides) which support approaches for missing data need to explicitly clarify whether these approaches are supported or not thus ensuring alignment with the corresponding business requirements for the specification.
Rationale: To ensure no ambiguity between the Agency’s FHIR Specifications and ones which may be adopted as dependencies, the overall position of the specification in relation to missing data must be made explicit and clear to implementers.

Title: [Missing Data & Suppressed Data] Support for Suppressed Data
Requirement: Support for suppressed data (i.e. where implementers need to exclude a value for a data element e.g. for privacy reasons) SHALL be based solely on the corresponding business and information requirements which the specification is based upon.
Rationale: The Agency’s FHIR Specifications provide implementable technical specifications for well understood business and clinical use cases and their supporting technical documentation. These use cases are very likely to be sensitive to any suppressed data on the overall solution being supported. Accordingly, it is not up to teams responsible for developing the FHIR Specification to decide how and where suppressed data should be supported.
Informative Note: Teams responsible for developing FHIR Specifications are encouraged to ensure teams responsible for business and information requirements are aware of available approaches to supporting suppressed data in FHIR.

Title: [Missing Data & Suppressed Data] Suppressed Data Support in Dependencies
Requirement: Specifications which depend on other FHIR specifications (or Implementation Guides) which support approaches for suppressed data need to explicitly clarify whether these approaches are supported or not thus ensuring alignment with the corresponding business requirements for the specification.
Rationale: To ensure no ambiguity between the Agency’s FHIR Specifications and ones which may be adopted as dependencies, the overall position of the specification in relation to suppressed data must be made explicit and clear to implementers.

Title: [Use of Terminology] Re-use of Existing Terminology
Requirement: The specification SHOULD leverage existing terminologies publicly available Nationally or Internationally.
Rationale: Reusing existing terminologies (ValueSets and CodeSystems) eliminates duplication and enhances interoperability.
Informative Note: Provide rationale if there is a deviation from this policy and, for any reason, a new terminology artifact needs to be created instead of reusing an existing one.

Title: [Use of Terminology] Preferred Binding Strength
Requirement:
Binding strength ‘preferred’ SHALL be used under the following conditions: 
If the parent Implementation Guide specifies the binding strength as ‘preferred’ and the derived Implementation Guide does not introduce any additional constraints, the binding remains at the ‘preferred’ level.
Rationale: This policy ensures consistency with the parent IG while allowing implementers flexibility in selecting appropriate codes, as ‘preferred’ bindings are recommendations rather than strict requirements.
Informative Note: If a biding is defined as ‘preferred’ in AU Core and the use case in the derived agency IG doesn’t imposes any further restrictions, then use ‘preferred’ in the derived IG.

Title: [Use of Terminology] Example Binding Strength
Requirement: The specification SHALL NOT use “example” binding strength.
Rationale: Binding strength ‘example’ provides no enforceable constraint on terminology, leading to inconsistent implementations, poor interoperability, and lack of conformance validation.
Informative Note: Appropriate binding strengths such as required, extensible, or preferred must be applied based on the use case to ensure semantic consistency and predictable data exchange.

Title: [Use of Terminology] Use of Code System Supplement
Requirement: The specification SHOULD consider using CodeSystem supplement to define any additional designations, relationships, and/or properties for the codes of any existing CodeSystem.
Rationale:
This helps supporting the followings: 
  • Add support for additional languages 
  • Add properties for user interfaces, priorities and ordering etc.
Informative Note: Here is the HL7 Link on Supplement: CodeSystem - FHIR v4.0.1

Title: [Use of Invariants] Invariant Id
Requirement:
The [name] of the invariant SHALL follow the format: inv-[sequence-number]-[element-name(optional)]-[short-name] 
Where: 
[sequence-number]: Invariant sequence number for the resource in context 
[element-name(optional)]: name of the element of the FHIR resource in case multiple invariants are applicable.  
[short-name]: an abbreviations or acronyms focusing on the invariant’s context
Rationale: A consistent naming pattern for invariants used in the specification promotes improved readability and interoperability.

Title: [Use of Invariants] Use of FHIRPath
Rationale:
Explicitly identifying the version of FHIRPath used in this specification is essential to ensure consistent interpretation, validation and evaluation of expressions across implementations. 

Without clear understanding on the FHIRPath versioning, implementers may apply incorrect logic, leading to interoperability issues and inconsistent results.
Informative Note: Highlight the FHIRPath version on the Home Page as a dependency to provide transparency to the implementers.

Title: [IG Template & Menu Items] IG Template
Requirement: All Implementation Guide (IG) projects SHALL apply the Agency approved IG template.
Rationale: To ensure uniformities are maintained across all Agency developed IGs and alignment to the framework is enforced.

Title: [IG Template & Menu Items] Plain Language Descriptions
Requirement: All Implementation Guide (IG) projects SHALL provide a non-technical plain language description of the IG which summarises the purpose of the IG.
Rationale: The purpose of the plain language description is to clearly communicate the purpose of the IG to readers of all levels of understanding.

Title: [IG Template & Menu Items] Menu Items
Requirement:
All Implementation Guide (IG) projects SHALL include the following top level menu items. 
Additional menu items can be added based on the requirement from specific use case. 
  • Home: Provide details on purpose, introduction, background and how to navigate the different section of Implementation Guide  
  • Conformance : Provide technical conformance requirements related to obligation, missing data, must-support. 
  • Guidance: General guidance on some concepts specifically used in the Implementation Guide 
  • Security and Privacy 
  • FHIR Artefacts : List down all the key FHIR artefacts (e.g.: Profiles, Extension, Terminologies etc). Provide a sub menu for each conformance resource type used in the IG. 
  • Examples: A dedicated menu for listing all the examples used in the IG. 
  • Support: Provide option to download the IG as a package and summarise any licencing details 
  • Change Log: provide a change log as per the policy statement: “Resource change history”. Where applicable, provide a cross-version comparisons summary.
Rationale: Maintaining a consistent list of menu items improves readability for implementers and ensures seamless navigation across the various sections of the Implementation Guides published by the Agency.
Informative Note: Depending on the use case, the project team responsible for publishing the Implementation Guide may add additional sections and subsections within the menu items outlined above.
